sources.entry: pynamodb - A Pythonic interface for Amazon DynamoDB.

summary.one_liner: PynamoDB is a Pythonic ORM-style interface for Amazon DynamoDB that lets you define models and query tables with simpler code than the raw DynamoDB API.
summary.what_it_does: Lets you define a Python class that maps to a DynamoDB table, with attributes declared as hash keys, range keys, or regular fields. Models can create tables, save and retrieve items, and run query and scan operations with filter conditions such as startswith and equality. Global and local secondary indexes are declared as classes attached to a model and can be queried the same way. Query and scan results are returned as automatically paginated iterators, and bulk operations paginate automatically. The README also shows how to point a model at DynamoDB Local via a host setting and how to enable table streams with a stream_view_type.
use_cases: Store and retrieve application records in DynamoDB from Python
Define DynamoDB table schemas as Python classes
Query DynamoDB tables with filter conditions
Use secondary indexes on DynamoDB tables
Develop and test against DynamoDB Local
Enable DynamoDB streams on a table
how_to_run: git clone or install from GitHub: pip install git+https://github.com/pynamodb/PynamoDB.git
Define a Model subclass with a Meta class specifying table_name
notable: Pythonic model classes with typed attributes (Unicode, Binary, JSON, Number, Set, UTC Datetime)
Query and scan with filter conditions written as Python expressions
Automatic pagination for queries, scans, and batch operations
Support for Global and Local Secondary Indexes declared inside the model
Stream view type configuration built into the model Meta
caveats: The README warns that UnicodeSetAttribute behavior changed incompatibly in versions 1.6.0 and 3.0.1, and points to upgrade docs
Tables must exist before use; create_table is the only table-creation path shown and the README says the table must exist before you can use it
